files.insight: An explicit no-interprocedural-optimization constraint prevents specialization even when forced. Keep user optimisation policy separate from semantic admissibility.
Noinline prevents inlining but does not prohibit cloning specialization; small functions can still benefit from bound function arguments. Do not conflate distinct optimization controls.
Function-level minimum-size objective blocks clone expansion in this fixture; code size and speed objectives must be explicit policy.
All minsize callsites suppress specialization even if the callee lacks a size attribute. Cost context belongs to the use site as well as the definition.
Mixed size objectives allow specialization for the unrestricted call while leaving the size-constrained call unchanged; one global callee flag loses this distinction.
Optimise-for-size callee avoids duplication. Separate size-oriented objective from legality and raw call-count heuristics.

A weak interposable definition may not be the executing definition, while ODR identity permits specialization. Ink imported/source definitions need exact binding; name equality alone grants no authority.

Known callsites can specialize even when external/address-taken uses prevent global argument constancy, but the original entry must remain for unknown callers. Distinguish local specialization eligibility from whole-function removal.
